clue.text: It is annoying when there is money in a book

indicators.note: the money is placed inside the book, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A complaint about finding cash tucked between the pages of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irksome or vexing causes bother, the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Kind of writing which makes a sport almost agreeable

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the synonym is lopped off

explanation.surface: Someone claims a certain script makes a game nearly pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union is the sport, abbreviated as it is on British sports pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes were the letters of old Germanic alphabets, so this describes that style of script.

clue.text: Not realising that there are hostilities taking place in the end of a month

indicators.note: the fighting happens within the month, so those letters go inside
only the latter part of the month's name is used, its opening letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone oblivious to a war going on at the close of a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of a month' means the month's name minus its opening letter, not its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ignorant of a fact has not grasped it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Plant which is to be removed from the public henceforth

indicators.note: the letters are extracted from the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A plant that must be taken away from public view from now on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be removed from' lifts the letters out of 'publIC HENceforth'.
explanation.definitionFit: This crusty growth of fungus and alga is loosely classed among plants.

clue.text: Vessel in which the prime minister will come in shortly

indicators.note: the statesman enters the word for 'shortly', so he sits inside it

parts.note: Pitt (elder or younger) was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: A ship the premier will board before long.
explanation.walkthrough: William Pitt the Younger was Britain's prime minister around 1800.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any container, here the bowl once provided for spitting.

clue.text: Animal which finds its master inflexible

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree title

explanation.surface: A creature notices its owner is rigid and unbending.
explanation.walkthrough: MA is Master of Arts, a crossword stand-in for 'master'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large guard dog breed is a kind of creature.

clue.text: Blustering fellows have a second to clean the shields

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Bluffers assign an assistant to polish the shields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like a helper; it is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaggering adventurers who brag and bluster are the swashbuckling type.

clue.text: Priests who are concerned with the beginner among heads

indicators.note: the pieces go amid the word for heads

parts.note: L stands for learner, a beginner

explanation.surface: Clergy who look after the novice in a group of leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate a British novice driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops and other high-ranking churchmen are senior clergy, close to priests.

clue.text: Plant for head of empire

definitions.meaning: a tall flowering bulb, Fritillaria imperialis

explanation.surface: A plant fit to crown an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tall fritillary flower, and also the regalia worn on an emperor's brow.

clue.text: Rod and adult for name of fish

parts.note: a wand is a slender rod
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: Fishing gear and a grown-up, plus a name for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Refers to the 1988 film comedy titled after a fish of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The film 'A Fish Called Wanda' gives its fish this name.

clue.text: A fellow securer of the payment makes money more certain

definitions.text: A fellow securer of the payment

explanation.surface: A partner underwriter makes cash safer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the long opening phrase; the wordplay is the short ending.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shares in underwriting a risk with another underwriter is a joint guarantor.

clue.text: Man caters unusually for a religious act

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an unusual way, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A man caters in an odd way for a church rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges MAN CATERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism and communion are rites of the church, sacred ceremonies.

clue.text: Fashionable rule for a relative

explanation.surface: Trendy regulation said to suit one of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A family member by marriage is a relation.

clue.text: A heavy drinker is a born leaker

parts.note: an oozer is something that seeps or leaks

explanation.surface: A tippler is a natural at dripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'born leaker' reads as 'natural blabber', but it is B + OOZER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sot or lush is someone who drinks a lot, slang for a toper.

clue.text: The adult behind the company appears in an exposed garment

indicators.note: the pieces show up inside the word for exposed
the adult follows the company, so its letter comes after

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up trailing the firm turns up in a revealing outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy coat worn over other clothes is an outer garment.

clue.text: Something thrown but in the confusion is it often caught?

definitions.text: Something thrown but in the confusion is it often caught?

parts.words: Something thrown but in the confusion is it often caught?
parts.note: describes paper scraps thrown over a newly married couple, which flutter about and are seldom caught

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a thrown object rarely caught in the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ball; it is the paper shower at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bits of coloured paper are tossed at weddings and land everywhere, so few are caught.

clue.text: Distress when the giver is involved in time

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the letters of the word giver

explanation.surface: Upset arises when a donor gets caught up over time.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve or wrong someone is to cause them pain, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Split which is almost pure against antiquity

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the synonym is cut

parts.note: V is short for versus, against
age means antiquity or great oldness

explanation.surface: A rift that is nearly innocent, set against old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last N from CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft or division is a split, as in the splitting of a crystal.

clue.text: A fool is among the girls, for they are not independent

indicators.note: the fool sits amid the girls, so one goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A clown among the girls, since none are free.
explanation.walkthrough: Val is a girl's name; two of them make the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal dependants owed service to a lord, so they lacked independence.

clue.text: A chance to put an animal back

indicators.note: back means the animal's name is read the other way

explanation.surface: An opportunity to return a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is only a link; 'back' alone signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Something even and unpredictable is a toss of a coin, an even chance.

clue.text: Perform in exaggerated fashion when one bit of play is followed by another

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket play
an act is a part of a stage play

explanation.surface: Hamming it up as one scene succeeds another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of play' gives a cricket OVER (six deliveries), then a theatre ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham it up is to perform with too much emphasis.

clue.text: Garment made of horn and stuck

parts.note: cor is French for horn, as in cor anglais

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing fashioned from horn and fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is the horn of 'cor anglais'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiffened undergarment is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Secures the hair

explanation.surface: Fastens the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastens with a bolt, and tresses or curls of hair.

clue.text: Rummager holds a drink as underground consumer

indicators.note: the rummager contains the drink inside it

explanation.surface: A forager with a cuppa feeds below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that feeds on plant roots eats below the soil.

clue.text: Duck under heights to discover a body

indicators.note: in a down clue the duck sits below the heights

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, O

explanation.surface: Ducking below the hilltops to find a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of nought; tors are rocky Dartmoor hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Brings to consciousness again when possibly aware what men are after

indicators.note: the men come after the jumbled word
possibly signals that the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Rouses someone, if one is aware what the fellows seek.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken is a typical man's name, so men become Kens.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse again from sleep restores awareness.

clue.text: Part of the body which is a little bit between adults

indicators.note: the scrap sits between the two adults

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult, twice
an ort is a scrap of food

explanation.surface: A small piece wedged between grown-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' sets ORT inside A and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery leaving the heart is an organ of the body.

clue.text: For show ring broadcasting organisation about prime minister's number

indicators.note: the station surrounds the number

parts.note: the British PM lives at No 10 Downing Street

explanation.surface: A ring and a TV station surround the premier's door number.
explanation.walkthrough: The British prime minister lives at 10 Downing Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy display or pretentious exhibition is ostentation.
